title: A ladder of AI proficiency: where this course sits
summary: The three proficiency tiers (Basic, Intermediate, Advanced), who each is for and what it covers, the three test questions, where BA5306 sits, and the ladder in a single career.

chunks.heading: Three tiers of AI proficiency
chunks.explanation_md:
AI education is often organised into **three broad proficiency tiers**, moving from **general literacy**, through **hands-on model-building**, to **advanced engineering and research**.

| Level | Who it is for |
|---|---|
| **Basic (AI Literacy)** | Professionals, students or officials with a **non-technical background** who need **working fluency** |
| **Intermediate (Builder / Practitioner)** | Students or practitioners who will **build or deploy simple models themselves** |
| **Advanced (Developer / Researcher)** | Aspiring **AI engineers and researchers** building **production-grade systems** |

The chapter says understanding this ladder helps you **calibrate expectations** for the course.

chunks.heading: What each tier covers
chunks.explanation_md:
The table's **representative content** for each tier:

- **Basic:** what AI is and where it is applied; **narrow AI**; core concepts of **data, algorithms, models, bias and ethics**; a first look at **NLP, computer vision and speech recognition**; **responsible AI and data privacy**; everyday tools such as **Google Colab, ChatGPT and Gemini**.
- **Intermediate:** data collection, cleaning and preprocessing; **supervised vs. unsupervised learning**; model training for **regression and classification**; introductory use of **Scikit-learn, TensorFlow and PyTorch**; working with CSV, image and text datasets; **validation, testing and overfitting**; applied projects such as crop-disease detection, traffic prediction or sentiment analysis.
- **Advanced:** deep learning architectures (**CNNs, RNNs, Transformers**); model optimisation (loss functions, gradient descent, hyperparameter tuning); advanced use of PyTorch, TensorFlow and HuggingFace; transfer learning, embeddings and **foundation models**; deployment via ONNX and APIs, including edge deployment; **MLOps**, versioning and reproducibility; large-scale applications such as chatbots, recommendation engines and autonomous systems.
chunks.exam_line: Basic: concepts, ethics and everyday tools; Intermediate: building simple models (supervised vs. unsupervised, Scikit-learn, overfitting); Advanced: deep learning architectures, optimisation, deployment and MLOps.

chunks.heading: Where BA5306 sits, and a quick test for any content
chunks.explanation_md:
BA5306 is designed to take you **confidently through the Basic tier** and **into the early stages of the Intermediate tier**. The goal is **working fluency and applied judgement**, not developer-level engineering skill. For students who want to go further, the syllabus's **Module 6** moves into **"Responsible AI and AI Specialisations"**.

A useful test for where a piece of course content sits:

- **Basic** asks: *"What is this and where is it used?"*
- **Intermediate** asks: *"How would I build or evaluate a simple version of this myself?"*
- **Advanced** asks: *"How would I optimise, scale, or deploy this in production?"*

Nearly everything in **Modules 1 to 3** sits at the **Basic** level by design. **Modules 4 to 5** move into **early Intermediate** territory through hands-on tool use, stopping well short of the engineering depth the Advanced tier needs.

chunks.heading: The ladder in a single career
chunks.explanation_md:
**Business example.** A **brand manager** might work entirely at the **Basic** tier: briefing an agency on AI-generated creative and judging its fit. The **data scientist** supporting her sits at the **Advanced** tier, fine-tuning the recommendation model behind a loyalty programme.

**Both roles are essential.** This course trains the first, and gives enough **Intermediate exposure** that the two can **speak the same language**.

The chapter's reflection question for you: using the three-level ladder, honestly place your own current AI skill level. What would move you one level up in the next six months?

flashcards.back: Basic (AI Literacy), Intermediate (Builder / Practitioner), Advanced (Developer / Researcher).

For non-technical professionals, students or officials needing working fluency: what AI is, narrow AI, data, algorithms, models, bias, ethics, a first look at NLP, computer vision and speech recognition, responsible AI, data privacy, tools like Google Colab, ChatGPT, Gemini.

For people who will build or deploy simple models: data preparation, supervised vs. unsupervised learning, regression and classification, Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, validation, testing, overfitting.
For aspiring AI engineers and researchers: CNNs, RNNs, Transformers, optimisation, HuggingFace, foundation models, deployment via ONNX and APIs, MLOps.
